title: Common distributions: Bernoulli, Binomial, Uniform, Gaussian

steps.label: What a distribution is
steps.pseudocode: A distribution lists the possible values and how likely each is. The probabilities add up to 1.

steps.label: Bernoulli: one yes-or-no
steps.pseudocode: Bernoulli(p): the value 1 has probability p and the value 0 has probability 1 - p.

steps.label: Binomial: count the successes
steps.pseudocode: Binomial(n, p): the number of successes in n independent Bernoulli trials.

steps.label: Uniform: no favorite
steps.pseudocode: Uniform on [0, 1]: the density is the same at every point of the range.

steps.label: Gaussian: the bell curve
steps.pseudocode: The Gaussian is highest at its mean and about 68% of its values lie within one standard deviation.

steps.label: The four side by side
steps.pseudocode: Each distribution has a mean that summarizes its center.
steps.python:
p = 0.3
print(p, round(10 * p, 1), 0.5, 0.0)   # means: Bernoulli 0.3, Binomial 3.0, Uniform 0.5, Gaussian 0.0

steps.label: Choosing a distribution
steps.pseudocode: Match the question about the data to the distribution that models it.

steps.label: Distributions inside ML models
steps.pseudocode: Models assume distributions for labels and noise.
